name: Hubbell Incorporated
moat_justification: Spec-in, code-certified products embedded in utility standards with real switching friction and proven pricing power, held through cycles; capped at 7 because the products are ultimately manufactured components exposed to large diversified rivals (Eaton, ABB, Legrand, AMETEK) and to utility/construction capex cycles, with no network effect.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Strong-moat (7/10) grid/electrical compounder with clean owner's earnings — but at $470.53 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 7.98%, weighted IV@15 $191.22); it would need to fall to about $191 to clear the hurdle.
moat_for: Spec-in position in utility standards and certified products — displacement is slow and risky for the buyer
Switching costs: low-cost, failure-critical components are not bought on price alone
Proven pricing power through cost inflation
Breadth across utility T&D and electrical (front- and behind-the-meter), 75+ brands
High cash conversion; OE positive 5 of last 5 years
moat_against: Large diversified rivals (Eaton, ABB, Legrand, AMETEK) with greater scale
Cyclical utility, construction and industrial end markets
Manufactured components — no network effect or recurring-revenue lock-in
Acquisition-led growth adds integration and leverage risk (NSI, $3.0B, closed Q2 2026)
